key_insight: Subquadratic sequence models can reduce the heavy cost of transformer attention while still handling complex dependencies, but their effectiveness depends on the architecture. This paper compares xLSTM, Mamba-2, and Gated DeltaNet to clarify which designs work best for challenging code-centric tasks.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the high computational and memory cost of transformer quadratic attention, and the lack of clear guidance on which subquadratic architectures are most effective for real sequence modeling tasks with long-range dependencies.
method: Benchmark three leading subquadratic architectures: xLSTM, Mamba-2, and Gated DeltaNet.
Evaluate them on difficult dependency-heavy settings, including code model pre-training and distillation from large language models.
Compare model behavior and performance to identify practical design principles for scalable sequence modeling.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work helps narrow the design space for efficient sequence models beyond Transformers. It provides evidence for choosing architectures that balance scalability and performance on long-context, code-oriented workloads.
visual_elements: Side-by-side architecture comparison diagram for xLSTM, Mamba-2, and Gated DeltaNet

Performance leaderboard or radar chart across dependency-heavy benchmarks
paper_title: On Subquadratic Architectures: From Applications to Principles
paper_authors: Anamaria-Roberta Hartl, Levente Zólyomi, David Stap, Pieter-Jan Hoedt, Niklas Schmidinger
